abstract: The Biane–Pitman–Yor theta fixed point has a double moment-generating-function pole, while its complete compressed-theta branching approximants are entire. An accepted boundary theorem describes their convergence inside the pole but leaves convergence of the actual pole masses and exterior exponential tilts open. We resolve these questions for every fixed positive source heat. A Hardy tail estimate retains the full negative-input interval and proves convergence of total boundary mass. The exact branching primitive then bootstraps every fixed exponential tilt and yields locally uniform convergence on the entire scaled plane, together with a finite-depth expanding-disk growth bound. We identify the limiting density with the classical bisection/Drmota density, with explicit source normalization. Preservation of coefficient-ratio order under the actual nonlinear iteration supplies a complex bound on a growing region. Applying that bound on the complete Cauchy circle proves a uniform coefficient limit and determines the high integer-moment transition at indices of order $\epsilon_n^{-1}$, where $\epsilon_n=(7/12)^{7n/17}$. It also gives smoothed density convergence and absolute convergence of boundary Mellin moments for imaginary parts $o(\epsilon_n^{-1/2})$. Exact finite-depth identities retain both scale endpoints, with an independent Gamma-law normalization control. The classical limiting functions are not claimed as new. The additional tilt in the original Mellin integral varies on a finer scale than the proved smoothing resolution. No original growing-height Mellin comparison, zero-preservation, or Riemann-hypothesis theorem is asserted.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: New consolidated paper following the scope review of the rejected Paper136 revision. The accepted source comparison and backward-tree limit are cited as inputs from136/v1; their duplicate proofs and certificate are omitted. Entire convergence and the uniform high-moment profile are stated together at the beginning, followed by tail control, exponential integrability, coefficient variation, and complete-circle inversion. Boundary Fourier/Mellin consequences remain together, with normalization identities moved to AppendixA. Classical bisection/Drmota attribution and the original-Mellin limitation are retained. Unrelated private signed-transport work is excluded.
title: Convergence across the pole and high moments of compressed theta branching
